cdp-app.notes: Serve is package.json:30-31 'electron-dev' verbatim, with the three levers the project ALREADY reads: CYBOFLOW_VITE_PORT (frontend/vite.config.ts:12, strictPort:true at :15), CYBOFLOW_CDP_PORT (package.json:31 -> --remote-debugging-port), CYBOFLOW_DIR (main/src/utils/cyboflowDirectory.ts:89). CYBOFLOW_DIR is mandatory, not hygiene: the single-instance lock is keyed on the userData path under it (main/src/index.ts:592-611), so without it this instance silently loses to the developer's own pnpm dev. No 'web' entry: the renderer cannot bootstrap standalone without preload-injected electronTRPC (docs/VISUAL-VERIFICATION-SETUP.md:27-32). Attestation is the strongest channel that exists in the UNMODIFIED tree: preload exposes electronAPI.getAppVersion (main/src/preload.ts:210) -> ipc/app.ts:9-11 -> app.getVersion(), so a match proves preload + IPC + a live main process, not merely an answering socket. It is NOT build-stamped and does NOT distinguish this instance from the developer's own running app; see rung 2 for the launch-token upgrade that does. 'expected' tracks package.json version and must be re-derived on a version bump.

native-screen.notes: Same serve as cdp-app: the OS chrome only exists while the app runs. attach:'cdp' is kept deliberately even though this modality captures via peekaboo, because it sets VERIFY_DRIVER_ATTACH_ONLY (verificationAgentRunner.ts:2123) and stops the driver launching a blank chromium that would screenshot the wrong surface. app='Electron', not 'Cyboflow': a pnpm dev launch is UNPACKAGED, so the OS app name is Electron (docs/VISUAL-VERIFICATION-SETUP.md:87). titlePattern derives from frontend/index.html <title>Cyboflow</title> - BrowserWindow (main/src/index.ts:796) sets no title: option and nothing in frontend/src writes document.title. This is the WEAKEST channel and cannot distinguish this instance from the developer's own Electron window; rung 2 proposes a distinguishing title.

levers.notes: cdpPortFlag is what 'electron .' receives (package.json:31); the runbook sets it indirectly via CYBOFLOW_CDP_PORT, which that script interpolates. dataDirEnv is CYBOFLOW_DIR and NOT --user-data-dir: the single-instance lock keys on the userData path derived from CYBOFLOW_DIR (main/src/index.ts:592-611), so --user-data-dir alone does not break the singleton.
